en.1: Harry Potter challenge family, thank you for joining me again today.
en.2: Did you have a good weekend?
en.3: Today we're reading just 3 pages — 7, 8, and 9.
en.5: Last time, Mr. Dursley felt something was off and came home, remember?
en.6: Today his wife brings out two cups of tea, and this quiet teatime begins — but it's actually a really tense psychological standoff.
en.7: Mr. Dursley carefully feels her out, asking, "You haven't heard from your sister, have you?" — and his wife suddenly turns sharp.
en.8: And that's when Mr. Dursley's heart sinks.
en.9: We know that feeling too, right — that thud when a bad feeling turns out to be right.
en.10: Here Rowling uses tense in a really sneaky way.
en.11: Mr. Dursley expecting "she's definitely going to be angry" happened even before the past, so it's wrapped in past perfect, while his wife actually looking angry is just written in simple past.
en.12: It shows the order — what happened first.
en.14: With just tense, she sets up a domino of anxiety and then knocks it right down.
en.15: And the way his wife drinks her tea isn't just drinking, either.
en.16: She purses her lips and sips it.
en.17: Her displeasure shows completely in the shape of her mouth.
en.18: And Mr. Dursley lies in bed unable to sleep, turning thought after thought over in his head.
en.19: It's nice how she uses the same word for tossing and turning his body and for turning things over in his mind.
en.20: "Well, there's no reason they'd come to us," he thinks, finally drifting off — and then Rowling drops in one line.
en.22: Ooh, doesn't that foreshadowing give you chills?
en.23: Alright, now let's step outside the house.
en.24: The cat on the wall doesn't move a muscle, like a statue.
en.25: Even when a car door slams, even when an owl swoops right overhead, it doesn't quiver.
en.26: Then, around midnight, a man suddenly appears on the corner.
en.29: "Appeared so suddenly and silently you'd have thought he'd just popped out of the ground" — you can really picture it, right?
en.30: A purple cloak, a silver beard long enough to tuck into his belt, blue eyes behind half-moon glasses.
en.32: He clicks a silver device to switch off the streetlamps one by one, then greets the cat on the wall.
en.33: And then the cat turns into a witch wearing square glasses — Professor McGonagall.
en.34: But this very proper woman looks ruffled, somehow.
en.35: What's going on, what's going on?
en.38: Now that the two wizards have finally met, aren't you curious what happens next?
en.39: Whether you're joining us for the first time today, you've been reading with us all along, or you paused and just came back — welcome, all of you.
en.42: This was Stella, see you again tomorrow.
